title: Textures & Material Maps
description: Apply images to materials, explore albedo maps, normal maps, and tiling.

slides.title: Textures – Painting with Pixels 🖼️
slides.content:
# Adding Detail without Extra Geometry

A **texture** is an image file (PNG, JPG, TGA, etc.) that you map onto a material's property.

- **Albedo Texture** – provides surface color detail (like a brick wall).
- **Normal Map** – a bluish image that fakes bumps and grooves, giving the illusion of depth.
- **Metallic/Smoothness Map** – greyscale images controlling metallic and roughness per‑pixel.
- **Height Map** – for parallax effects.

To use a texture, simply drag it into the appropriate slot in the material Inspector.

quizData.question: What does a Normal Map do?

options.text: Adds actual geometry to the model
Fakes surface bumps and details using lighting

quizData.explanation: Normal maps alter the surface normals per pixel, simulating bumps without extra polygons.

slides.title: Tiling & Offset 🔁
slides.content:
# Repeating Textures

- **Tiling** (X, Y) – how many times the texture repeats across the surface. 1 = no repeat, 2 = twice in that axis.
- **Offset** (X, Y) – slides the texture position. Useful for scrolling effects.

Example: A brick wall texture with tiling (2,2) will show four times as many bricks in the same area.

quizData.question: If you set tiling to (3, 1), what happens to the texture?

options.text: It repeats 3 times horizontally, but not vertically

quizData.explanation: Tiling X = 3 repeats the texture 3 times along the U (horizontal) axis.

slides.title: Import Settings for Textures ⚙️
slides.content:
# Texture Import Config

When you select a texture in the Project window, the Inspector shows import settings:

- **Texture Type** – Default, Normal Map, Sprite, etc. Choose **Normal Map** for normal maps to get special compression.
- **Alpha Source** – if the image has transparency.
- **Max Size** – limits resolution to save memory (e.g., 512, 1024).
- **Compression** – reduces file size for builds.
- **Generate Mip Maps** – creates smaller versions for distant objects (leave on for most cases).

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Proper Normal Map Import

Always set a normal map texture's **Texture Type** to **Normal Map** in the import settings. Unity will then handle it correctly for lighting and compression.
